text:
Justin Hryckowian was one of the nice stories of Dallas's last season: undrafted out of Northeastern, 30 points in 81 games and, per Evolving-Hockey, a full win above replacement. Year two has been slower. He has three points in 19 games on 15 minutes a night, though the Stars did give him the full "The Franchise" feature treatment on Nov. 9.

The early season isn't all luck this time. His chance rate is down from 0.73 individual expected goals per 60 to 0.53, and Dallas gets 47% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, six points worse than without him. He's shooting 9.5%, a little under his norm, so a goal or two is owed, but not a flood.

His game leans on the forecheck: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 30% of his entries last season, and he plays like Casey Cizikas, a dump-and-chase grinder. He has 36 hits already. He's had a few more looks over his last three games, and he picked up an assist in Saturday's 2-0 win over Buffalo. That's the trend worth watching.
